mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the triggered instances, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3 percentage points within a month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth by more than 1% over two quarters signals a weakening demand environment, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the periods following a GDP decline, or the correlation between GDP decline and negative 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 2% over two months signals a strengthening supply side, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the triggered instances, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4.5% and the CPI is increasing by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals an inflationary environment with tight monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
regime_hint: inflationary environment with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances, or the joint effect of high FEDFUNDS and rising CPI on negative 5-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 300,000 in a month and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points, it signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 300k in 1 month and UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the triggered instances, or the joint effect of strong PAYEMS and declining UNRATE on positive 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts by more than 10% over two months signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the triggered instances, or the correlation between a decline in HOUST and negative 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail and food services sales by more than 1% over three months signals a strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods following a RSAFS increase, or the correlation between RSAFS increase and positive 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
